I farm 6 mu, and I do not spread money around blindly. I start from what worked before, then I adjust a little. On my land, with well water, I will keep fertilizer a bit on the safe side, because if yield drops, that hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. I have only primary school, so I do it in a simple way: I look at my own field, I look at what the neighbors got last year, and I ask the seed and fertilizer seller what people nearby are using. For wheat and maize, I will stay with the kind of management we know well in Hebei: decent base fertilizer, then topdressing when the crop is really taking off. For stevia, I will watch water and potassium more carefully, because if leaves do not grow well, there is no money in it. Since some people in my family work off-farm, I will not choose a plan that needs too much hand labor all at once. I will split the 6 mu as 2 mu wheat, 2 mu maize, and 2 mu stevia, keep irrigation steady, and not cut pesticide too much if I see pressure early.
